text_blocks.snippet: The boiling point of water is 212°F (212 degrees Fahrenheit) at standard sea-level atmospheric pressure.
Factors That Change the Boiling Point

list.snippet: Altitude: Higher elevations have lower air pressure, which makes water boil at lower temperatures. For example, water boils at about 202°F in Denver and around 160°F to 165°F on Mount Everest.
Dissolved Minerals or Salt: Adding substances like salt to water raises the boiling point slightly.
Pressure: Increasing external pressure (such as when using a pressure cooker) raises the boiling temperature of water.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about how elevation changes cooking times through the ThermoWorks Boiling Point Calculator.
